Returns a checksum value based on the current record in the current work area. You can use a checksum to test the validity of data. You can also generate checksum values greater than 16 bits for large strings.

[[T0]](2017) offers complementary functionality to [[T1]](2007) - Checksum Value.

[[C0]]

**[[T0]]**
Specifies a comma-delimited list, with or without spaces, containing one or more fields to exclude from the checksum calculation. The maximum length of the field string is limited to 256 characters. If [[T1]] is empty, [[T2]] does not exclude fields except for Memo and General fields.
**[[T3]]**
Specifies a numeric seed value of 0 that is used to calculate the checksum and is included for backward compatibility. Passing a value of -1 for [[T4]] uses the default system value of 0. For [[T5]] calculations, [[T6]] disregards [[T7]] .
**[[T8]]**
Specifies additive bit values for generating the checksum. Versions of [[T9]] earlier than 8.0 used a [[T10]] 16-bit algorithm to calculate the checksum values of strings. [[T11]] now includes the [[T12]] routine to calculate larger 32-bit values. You can control the setting of this algorithm by setting the first bit value of the [[T13]] parameter. The following table lists the bit values you can add to produce a value for [[T14]] . Value Bits Description 1 001 Calculate checksum value using [[T15]] checksum algorithm. 2 010 Include Memo fields in the checksum calculation. You can use the second [[T16]] bit to include Memo fields in the [[T17]] calculation. [[T18]] includes all Memo fields except any specified by [[T19]] in the calculation. The following table lists the possible values for [[T20]] , produced by the sum of the bit flags. [[T21]] Description 0 Calculate checksum based on [[T22]] parameter using [[T23]] checksum algorithm. (Default) 1 Calculate checksum based on [[T24]] parameter using [[T25]] checksum algorithm. 2 Calculate checksum based on current record contents including Memo fields using [[T26]]. 3 Calculate checksum based on current record contents including Memo fields using [[T27]].

When calculating the checksum value from the current record, [[T0]] disregards Memo and General fields unless [[T1]] is set to 2 or 3.

[[T2]] generates the checksum based on the current record in the current work area and passes the byte values of the string into the [[T3]] routine.

[[T4]] returns a value of "0" if no cursor is open in the current work area or if the record pointer is not valid, for example, pointing to a phantom record.

When you create a string expression from a record, [[T5]] removes trailing blank spaces and returns the expression as a character string, similar to the [[T6]] function.

Usually, [[T7]] uses any excluded fields specified by [[T8]] to store the checksum value and does not include them in the calculation. [[T9]] does not perform any checks on the data type of these fields. If [[T10]] contains an invalid field, [[T11]] disregards that field.

[[T12]] calculates the checksum from all the fields included except for Memo, General, and those specified by [[T13]]. You can determine the fields used and their order using the [[T14]] function. If you specified a setting for [[T15]], the checksum is calculated based on the current list specified by [[T16]] which could include calculated fields.

textos.91ed2ca5-3f9c-4641-b2fd-07b1c341a78c#108: A [[T0]] Project object exposes the IDispatch interface so that Automation clients, ActiveX controls, and other [[T1]] objects can access the project object through standard [[T2]] interfaces. When manipulating projects, errors that might occur are [[T3]] errors because a Project object exposes the IDispatch interface.
The following sections describe events and the order in which they occur when projects are created, modified, closed, built, and so on.

The following events occur when you execute [[T0]], create a new project from the File menu, or click the New button on the standard toolbar to create a new project:
 - The Project object is created.
- The ProjectHook object instantiates.
- The Init event for the ProjectHook object occurs. If the Init event returns true ([[T1]]), the default, the project is created and the project is displayed in the Project Manager. If the Init event returns false ([[T2]]), the project isn't created, the project and ProjectHook objects are released, and the Project Manager isn't displayed.

The following events occur when you execute [[T0]], modify an existing project from the File menu, or click the Open button on the standard toolbar to open an existing or create a new project:
 - The project object is created. The project object obtains its values from the project's .pjx file.
- The ProjectHook object is instantiated.
- The Init event for the ProjectHook object occurs. If the Init event returns true ([[T1]]) (the default), the project is opened for modification in the Project Manager. If the Init event returns false ([[T2]]), the project isn't opened for modification, the project and ProjectHook objects are released, and the Project Manager isn't displayed.

The following events occur when an open project is closed:
 - The ProjectHook Destroy event occurs and the ProjectHook object is released.
- The Project object is released.

The following events occur when [[T0]], [[T1]], or [[T2]] is issued:
 - The project object is created. The project object obtains its values from the project's .pjx file.
- The ProjectHook object is instantiated.
- The Init event for the ProjectHook object occurs. If the Init event returns true ([[T3]]), the default, the ProjectHook BeforeBuild event occurs. If [[T4]] is included in the BeforeBuild event, the .app, .dll, or .exe isn't built. Otherwise, the build process continues. If any files are added to the project during the build process, the ProjectHook QueryAddFile event occurs before each file is added. If [[T5]] is included in the QueryAddFile event, a file isn't added to the project. Otherwise, the file is added to the project. When the .app, .dll, or .exe is successfully built, the ProjectHook AfterBuild event occurs, and then the ProjectHook Destroy event occurs. If the Init event returns false ([[T6]]), the app, .dll, or .exe isn't built, and the project and ProjectHook objects are released.

The following events occur when [[T0]] with the [[T1]] clause is issued. If the [[T2]] clause is omitted, the events occur in the order described above when [[T3]], [[T4]], or [[T5]] is issued.
 - The project object is created. The project object obtains its values from the project's .pjx file.
- The ProjectHook object is instantiated.
- The Init event for the ProjectHook object occurs. If the Init event returns true ([[T6]]), the default, the files specified in the [[T7]] clause are added individually to the project. The ProjectHook QueryAddFile event occurs before each file is added to the project. If [[T8]] is included in the QueryAddFile event, the file isn't added to the project. Otherwise, the file is added to the project. The ProjectHook BeforeBuild event then occurs. If [[T9]] is included in the BeforeBuild event, the project isn't built. Otherwise, the project is built.
- When the project build is complete, the ProjectHook AfterBuild event occurs, and then the ProjectHook Destroy event occurs. If the ProjectHook Init event returns false ([[T10]]), the project isn't built. The project and ProjectHook objects are released and a new .pjx file isn't created.

The following events occur when you drag a file or a set of files over the outline section (treeview) of the Project Manager:
 - When the mouse pointer is positioned over the outline section of the Project Manager, the ProjectHook OLEDragOver event occurs with the [[T0]] parameter set to 0 ([[T1]] in [[T2]]). The OLEDragOver event then occurs repeatedly with the [[T3]] parameter set to 2 ([[T4]] in [[T5]]). If the mouse pointer moves outside of the outline section of the Project Manager, the OLEDragOver event occurs with the [[T6]] parameter set to 1 ([[T7]] in [[T8]]).
- The ProjectHook OLEDragDrop event occurs if you release the mouse button while the mouse pointer is positioned over the outline section of the Project Manager. By default, [[T9]] adds each file dropped on the Project Manager to the project. The ProjectHook QueryAddFile event occurs before each file is added to the project.
